slice: Suzuki RM-Z450 (2018 generation) and RM-Z250 (2019 generation) from magazine race tests 2019-2025: platform history, dyno and weight against rivals, tester settings, couplers and app, known problems and fixes (knowledge push 2026-11)

records.statement: The current RM-Z450 arrived for 2018 with new bodywork, frame and the Showa coil fork and BFRC shock. For 2019 the shock spring went from 56 to 54 N/mm with new damping, and the bike came with three plug-in couplers. Magazine testers found the 2020-2023 bikes unchanged. The engine's only updates in the previous decade were the launch and traction functions added for 2016. It is kickstart only. List price $8,999 in 2023, $600 to $2,000 less than its rivals.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.topic: RM-Z450 dyno by rpm and weight
records.statement: On a magazine dyno the RM-Z450 made 45.9 hp at 7,000 rpm, 52.4 hp at 8,000 rpm and peaked at 54.39 hp at 8,800-8,900 rpm, the lowest peak in the class; at 11,000 rpm it was 7.5 hp behind the Yamaha, KTM, Honda and Husqvarna. It weighed 241 lb without fuel, the heaviest 450, nearly 20 lb more than the lightest. It is brisk off the bottom and strongest from 7,000 to 8,800 rpm, then falls away above 9,000, so it is best short-shifted.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.statement: A magazine test crew's RM-Z450 fork setup (Showa 49 mm coil): stock 0.50 kg/mm springs, compression 10 clicks out (stock 6; testers ranged from 7 to 12), rebound 12 out, legs lowered to about flush in the clamps to slow the steering and calm head shake, and 10 cc of oil added to each leg to firm the last part of the stroke.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.statement: A magazine test crew's RM-Z450 shock setup (Showa BFRC, which has no high-speed compression adjuster): stock 54 N/mm spring, compression 1 turn out (stock 1-1/2), rebound 1 turn out (stock 3), race sag 105-108 mm, with a shock link 1 mm longer than the stock 135 mm one. The longer link lowers the high-riding rear and firms the first part of the stroke.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.statement: Stock gearing on the RM-Z450 is 13/50. Testers kept it in 2019 and later moved to 13/51 to reach third gear sooner.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.topic: RM-Z450 couplers, app and holeshot assist
records.statement: The RM-Z450 comes with three plug-in couplers: stock, aggressive (sharper throttle, slightly lean on top, suited to tight supercross-style tracks) and mellow. Testers raced the stock one. Suzuki's MX-Tuner 2.0 phone app adds four preset maps and custom maps with 36 editable cells; loading a map needs the connector, data cable and a separate 12 V battery. Holeshot assist (S-HAC) has three modes on the launch button.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.topic: RM-Z450 weak points and fixes from race tests
records.statement: Repeated tester findings on the 2018-generation RM-Z450: the clutch slips (three stiffer springs can be enough; a complete aftermarket clutch is the full cure), the chain guide wears (aftermarket guide), the 1.1 radiator cap lets it boil over (a 1.8 or 2.0 cap), the front brake is grabby with poor feel, the BFRC shock steps out when the wheels go light (a specialist rebuild, or the conventional RM-Z250 shock), the fork moves too fast in the mid-stroke then spikes (revalve), and the rear rides high, which makes it oversteer and shake at speed until it is lowered.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.topic: RM-Z450 handling and how to balance it
records.statement: The RM-Z450 has the sharpest turn-in of the 450s but is unstable at speed as delivered. The magazine recipe: lower the rear (the softer 2019-on spring, 105-110 mm sag and a 1 mm longer link), then slide the fork down to flush. That gives more room to tune compression, rebound and fork height. Its 2019 peak of 54.39 hp compared with 60.21 for the CRF450R, 57.51 YZ450F, 57.14 450 SX-F, 56.40 FC 450 and 55.86 KX450.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.statement: The usual answers to the RM-Z450's missing top end are an aftermarket exhaust and one more tooth on the rear sprocket; testers did not publish measured gains.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2023 Suzuki RM-Z450 race test

records.statement: The current RM-Z250 dates from 2019: a new head with reshaped intake ports and a more aggressive intake cam, dual injectors (one under the throttle body, one in the airbox inlet), an air-cleaner opening 30% larger, new second-gear and final ratios, a frame 0.8 lb lighter with 10% more torsional stiffness, a hex-rail aluminium subframe, a lighter swingarm, Kayaba coil-spring fork in place of the PSF-2 air fork with a Kayaba shock, a 270 mm front disc, D.I.D DirtStar rims, Dunlop MX33 tyres and footpegs moved slightly forward and up. Testers found it unchanged from 2020 through 2025. It has a five-speed gearbox and no electric start.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2019 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.topic: RM-Z250 dyno and weight against the class
records.statement: On a magazine dyno the RM-Z250 made 39.0 hp in 2022 and 39.52 hp in 2025, against about 44-45 hp for the KTM, Husqvarna, GasGas and Kawasaki 250s. It weighed 226-227 lb without fuel. It matches the best from 5,000 to 7,500 rpm and is friendly from about 6,000 to 9,000, then falls behind and needs short-shifting. It also vibrates more than its rivals. List price $7,899 in 2022 and $8,199 in 2025, with dealers often discounting $1,000-1,500.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.statement: The RM-Z250's stock 5.0 N/mm fork springs are too stiff for most riders. A magazine test crew's setup: 4.7-4.9 N/mm springs, compression 14 clicks out (stock 11), rebound 13 out, standard fork height. If the stock springs stay: compression fully out and the oil lowered by 20-30 in each leg, unless the rider is around 200 lb.

values.stock_spring_fix: comp full out, oil down 20-30 per leg

source.name: Motocross Action - 2022 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.statement: A magazine test crew's RM-Z250 shock setup: a 50 N/mm spring in place of the stock 52, race sag 107 mm (stock 105-110), high-speed compression (blue) 14 clicks out, low-speed compression (silver) 14 out, high-speed rebound (bottom) 16 out, low-speed rebound (red) 14 out. With stock springs the crew ran 104 mm of sag to put weight on the fork.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2022 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.statement: The RM-Z250 has three plug-in couplers; the white one is the most aggressive off the bottom and every magazine tester chose it, while the grey one is smoother and slower to pick up. The MX-Tuner 2.0 app has four presets (aggressive, smooth, richer, leaner) and custom maps. A tuner map written for an aftermarket exhaust ran noticeably better than stock in testing even on the stock pipe. Testers found launch control of no use on a 39 hp bike.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.topic: RM-Z250 weak points and fixes from race tests
records.statement: Repeated tester findings on the 2019-generation RM-Z250: clutch friction plates wear fast and it slips within a few hours of hard use (stiffer springs), the fork is supercross-stiff, the gearbox is notchy when shifted under load, the front brake is weak and fades, and it is the heaviest and least powerful bike in the class with no electric start. On the other side, testers logged 50-plus hours a year on these bikes since 2019 with no serious failures.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.topic: RM-Z250 what power mods are worth
records.statement: On the RM-Z250 a good full exhaust is worth about 2 hp for roughly $1,000. Testers estimated $4,000 or more in porting, cam, piston, pipe and ignition work to match a stock Austrian 250, and one heavily modified RM-Z250 only equalled a stock KX250. Aftermarket engine mounts (about $430) were tried to soften the stiff chassis feel.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2025 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test

records.statement: The RM-Z250 is built to turn: once the fork is softened it is the best-cornering 250 and holds a line without standing up. The cost is stability: it can oversteer on entry, tuck in tight corners and shake on fast, rough straights, and it is harsh on hard, choppy tracks with the stock fork. The cockpit is compact and suits smaller riders.

source.name: Motocross Action - 2022 Suzuki RM-Z250 race test
